items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 24% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: There is no rule that says the bad news gets priced in quickly. It is, sometimes, a process that takes very long. The current phase is probably like that – a slow and long-drawn downturn. You know, of course, that it will pass, but you cannot say when. And it is the waiting that tests everyone's patience.

items.title: Tata Sons IPO: How 7 Tata Group stocks performed this week amid IPO buzz
items.description: Tata Group stocks witnessed sharp volatility this week as developments around the Tata Sons IPO triggered strong buying and selling. Tata Chemicals led the gains with a 13% rise, while Tata Investment Corp gained 8%. Tata Power, IHCL and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles also ended higher despite Friday’s sell-off.

items.title: Stock split alert! 3 stocks turning ex-record date for stock splits next week. Do you own any?
items.description: As many as three companies have fixed their record dates for their stock splits next week. While the number of outstanding shares increases during a stock split, the company’s overall market capitalisation remains unchanged. A lower share price can make the stock more accessible to retail investors, potentially improving participation and trading volumes.

items.title: Tata Group stocks reel from aftershocks as Trusts opposes third term for N Chandra
items.description: Tata stocks plummeted on Friday due to opposition from Tata Trusts, who contested the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman by the Tata Sons board. This leadership tug-of-war has raised concerns among investors, uncertain about its implications for multiple group companies. The potential for Tata Sons to go public remains a pivotal opportunity for stakeholders, with future resolutions between the board and Trusts likely affecting market sentiment.

items.title: HFCL, Polycab India among 7 companies that are Goldman Sachs’ AI enablers. See full list
items.description: India’s stock market may be masking a powerful AI opportunity. While the Nifty has declined 12% in 2026, AI-linked companies have surged as demand rises for the power, data centres and semiconductor infrastructure needed to support the global AI build-out. Here are five power-generation stocks that Goldman Sachs says are AI-enablers.

items.title: Ashish Kacholia's Portfolio: 10 stocks rally up to 180% in CY26, 4 turn multibaggers; 1 new Q1 bet
items.description: Investors closely monitor the portfolios of prominent market participants on Dalal Street. In this context, ETMarkets analysed the investment holdings of well-known investor Ashish Kacholia. According to the latest data for the June 2026 quarter, Kacholia publicly disclosed stakes in around 33 stocks. The total portfolio value was estimated at roughly Rs 3,102 crore as of September 18, 2026, up about 19% from Rs 2,602 crore in the December 2025 quarter. Notably, the list includes only companies in which Kacholia holds a stake of more than 1%, and therefore may not represent his entire portfolio.A deeper analysis shows that around 15 of these stocks have delivered more than 25% returns so far in CY26. Of these, 10 stocks have gained between 40% and 180%, while four have more than doubled, turning into multibaggers and significantly increasing investors' wealth. The analysis also identified one stock that was newly added to the portfolio during the June 2026 quarter. (Data Source: ACE Equity, Trendlyne).

items.title: Concurrent Gainers: 10 smallcap stocks that gain for 5 days in a row
items.description: Over the five trading sessions ending September 18, the benchmark Sensex declined 0.81%, or 608 points, to close at 74,295. The index ended lower in four of the five sessions between September 11 and September 18. Despite the market weakness, 10 stocks from the BSE SmallCap Index recorded gains in all five sessions. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Can Nifty defend the 23,000 support zone?
items.description: Nifty enters the week in a corrective, range-bound setup, with 23,000–23,100 emerging as crucial support and 23,500 as the first resistance. Weak momentum indicators and subdued volatility suggest cautious trading. A sustained move above 23,500 could support a rebound, while a break below 23,000 may deepen the correction.
